# Trading research and development
Read the current project's strategy and AGENTS.md before implementing. Dakota's Periscope work uses notifications as its execution boundary unless he explicitly changes the project scope. Never turn research into brokerage orders or store broker credentials by inference.
Use connected market data and primary broker/exchange documentation, timestamp observations, and distinguish real-time, delayed, historical and simulated data. For stock OHLC exercises use only stock data; do not imply options profitability. Document bar interval, session/timezone, adjustments, missing data and look-ahead prevention. Use chronological development and held-out periods, include costs/slippage, intrabar stop/target ambiguity, position sizing and portfolio constraints. Report drawdown, expectancy, win rate, trade log and sample size. Compare to a clearly specified benchmark. Do not call a strategy proven because a historical simulation performs well. Research open-source engines through article-discovery.md, inspect licenses and reproducibility, then implement only the requested scope.
